intent: Bring code_tutor/_challenge_support.py under the 250-line cap by moving the isolated pytest runner and the LLM verdict streaming into their own modules, with no behaviour change.
scope: python_pkg/code_tutor/tests/test_challenge.py, test_challenge_part2.py, test_challenge_part3.py (import and patch paths only)
Non-goal: no assertion changed, no test deleted, skipped or weakened
changes: Moved _pytest_clean and _patch_and_test into _pytest_runner.py, which now owns the subprocess, os and sys imports they were the only users of, and imports _project_root back from _challenge_support.
Moved _stream_verdict and _parse_verdict into _verdict.py, which owns rich.live.Live, Text, time, json and re. Live was used at exactly one call site, so nothing else in _challenge_support needed it.
_challenge_support.py dropped seven now-dead imports (Live, Text, time, json, os, subprocess, sys, re) and keeps ast, Path, Panel and Syntax, which its remaining source-inspection helpers use.
_challenge.py imports the four moved functions back from their new homes, preserving the patch targets test_challenge_part3.py names on _challenge.

Repointed the test patch strings per name: ten occurrences of _challenge_support.Live to _verdict.Live, three of _challenge_support.subprocess.run and two of _challenge_support._pytest_clean to _pytest_runner. Also repointed the direct imports in test_challenge.py and test_challenge_part2.py.

verification.evidence: 216 passed before the split and 216 passed after it - identical pass count, not merely a green run.

Two intermediate failures, both caught by running rather than by reading: first 2 collection ImportErrors because test_challenge.py and test_challenge_part2.py import the moved functions directly, then 5 failures with 'does not have the attribute _pytest_clean' and 'no attribute subprocess' from patch strings still naming the old module. Both fixed per name.

verification.command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c "from python_pkg.code_tutor import _challenge as c, _challenge_support as s, _pytest_runner as r, _verdict as v; c._pytest_clean; c._patch_and_test; c._stream_verdict; s.Syntax; s.ast; r.subprocess; r.os; r.sys; v.Live; v.time"
verification.evidence: runtime probe OK - every patched name is a real attribute of the module its test names.
237, 111 and 89 lines, all under the 250-line cap. The first cut alone left 313, so a second seam was needed - the budgeting warning in docs/python-split-recipes.md again.

verification.command: pre-commit run --files <the touched files and artifacts>
verification.evidence: ruff, ruff format, mypy, pylint, bandit and pytest-with-coverage all pass on the touched files.

risks: A sed with escaped alternation silently matched nothing and left the patch strings unchanged while reporting success; the failing test run caught it and the replacement was redone in Python. Worth remembering that a no-op rewrite looks identical to a successful one at the shell.

_pytest_runner runs the user's tests in a subprocess. Its subprocess import is patched by test_challenge.py, so a future move of that import would let the suite really invoke pytest - the same silent-failure shape as the CUPS restart in brother_printer.
rollback: git revert the commit; _challenge_support.py returns to 402 lines and the two new modules disappear.
After rollback, re-run the package suite and confirm it still reports 216 passed.
